description: Phase locked loop: a square wave oscillator, a phase comparator against an incoming signal, and a low pass filter that steers the oscillator.

params.text: Sets the oscillator frequency in semitones either side of C4 at 261.63Hz, 54 semitones each way.
Sets the pulse width of the oscillator, 1% to 100%; the default is 50%.
Scales the voltage arriving at the PWM input, 0 to 100%; at zero that input does nothing.
Sets the cutoff of the four pole low pass filter, 15Hz to 8400Hz; low settings warble and high settings run wild.
Puts out 5V while exactly one of the two signals is above 0V and -5V otherwise.
Runs the two signals into a D type flip-flop built from four nand gates, and puts out 5V or -5V from its state.
Puts out 5V while the signal is ahead, -5V while the square wave is ahead, and 0V while they agree.
Takes the larger of the two input voltages less the smaller, a fuzzy logic exclusive-or after Lotfi Zadeh.
Takes a fuzzy exclusive-or built on hyperbolic parabolas, so the output bends rather than stepping.

inputs.text: Moves the oscillator frequency at a volt per octave; with nothing patched here the filter output steers the oscillator instead.
Moves the pulse width of the oscillator, scaled by the PWM CV knob.
Replaces the internal square wave going into the phase comparator; the oscillator itself keeps running.
The signal the comparator measures against the square wave; a square-ish wave works best.
Moves the filter cutoff, 5V covering its whole range.

outputs.text: The square wave from the internal oscillator, swinging between -5V and 5V.
The output of whichever comparator is selected.
The filtered comparator output; with nothing patched to the oscillator's FM input, this is what steers the oscillator.

notes: the filter output is normalled to the oscillator's FM input, which is what closes the loop; patching anything into that FM input breaks the loop open.

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
